purpose: Qualification test catalogue, not a runtime definition format.
evidence_policy: Attach executed test identifiers and durable observations; source reading alone is not a pass.

cases.title: Text turn lifecycle
assertions: A user message precedes one assistant response and one turn end.
The completion event follows the finalized assistant message.
Awaited observers finish before the public run promise settles.

cases.title: Tool round trip
assertions: Each call has one correlated result before the next model request.
A final text response stops natural continuation.
Tools execute only after the requesting assistant message is finalized.

cases.title: Streaming protocol
assertions: Text, thinking and tool-call deltas remain observable without executing partial calls.
The terminal message replaces partial content instead of duplicating it.
A response without start events still produces one finalized message.

cases.title: Parallel and sequential tools
assertions: Parallel preflight follows call order; admitted tools can overlap.
Completion events reflect completion order; persisted results retain call order.
One sequential-only tool makes the entire batch sequential.

cases.title: Tool admission and failures
assertions: Argument preparation precedes schema validation and admission.
Unknown, malformed, denied and throwing tools become error results without unintended effects.
Nested tool access crosses the same validation and authorization boundary.

cases.title: Truncated tool calls
assertions: A length-limited assistant message executes none of its tool calls.
Synthetic failures retain call associations and permit a later corrected request.

cases.title: Cancellation
assertions: Cancellation reaches model and active tool actors through AbortSignal.
Unstarted sequential calls do not execute after cancellation.
Late events cannot restart the completed run or corrupt its next invocation.

cases.title: Steering and follow-up queues
assertions: Steering enters at the next turn boundary, not between tools in a batch.
Follow-up input waits until natural work settles.
One-at-a-time and all-message delivery preserve queue order.
An input arriving during turn preparation is not lost or delivered twice.

cases.title: Turn finalization decisions
assertions: End stops before polling queues.
Continue causes exactly one next request unless natural continuation already supplies it.
Error and aborted responses remain hard exits.
All finalized tool results must request termination to suppress automatic tool continuation.

cases.title: Continue existing context
assertions: Empty and system-only contexts reject without consuming queues.
A non-assistant tail retries existing context before follow-ups.
An assistant tail selects steering before follow-up instead of sending an invalid tail.

cases.title: Lifecycle ownership and budgets
assertions: Visible native machine states own continuation, cancellation and termination.
Model and tool actors perform bounded operations, not hidden agent loops.
A configured turn budget returns explicit control rather than looping indefinitely.

cases.title: Model projection boundary
assertions: Request preparation precedes transformContext and conversion to model messages.
Projection preserves roles, tool associations and compatible media.
Custom host messages can be omitted without deleting durable history.

cases.title: Dynamic tools and model selection
assertions: Tool declarations match the executable set after additions and removals.
Per-request model and reasoning selection affect the next request without corrupting prior turns.
A removed capability cannot be invoked through stale model context.

cases.title: Compaction threshold and cut
assertions: Compaction triggers only above the configured threshold.
The kept suffix does not orphan tool results from calls.
A split user-message span retains a coherent recent suffix.

cases.title: Compaction continuity
assertions: Repeated compaction includes the previous summary and newly summarized retained history.
The summary plus retained suffix becomes the next request context.
Raw history remains inspectable after compaction.
Compaction cancellation or failure does not install an incomplete summary.

cases.title: Extension lifecycle
assertions: Input interception can handle or transform input before the run.
Before-run and context hooks affect the intended request in declared order.
Tool admission and result hooks can deny or replace results.
A failed hook has an explicit failure path; stale extension contexts cannot affect a replaced session.

cases.title: Resource ownership
assertions: Two instances isolate local stores and deliberately share only declared services.
Lifetime boundaries dispose owned resources without disposing shared resources.
Resource access does not automatically expose resource data to the model.

cases.title: Context provenance and data states
assertions: Prepared context records source identities, ordering and transformations.
Missing, empty, stale and failed data remain distinguishable.
Inspection reports the exact sent context without leaking undeclared resources.

cases.title: Provider hooks and observations
assertions: Provider request and stream adapters expose controlled transformation and observation seams.
A request transformation does not silently mutate durable messages.
Usage, tool associations and terminal outcomes survive observation hooks.

cases.title: Independent child machines
assertions: A root invokes two instances with distinct inputs and observes both outputs.
Advancing one instance leaves the other state and input unchanged.

cases.title: Cycles, nesting and parallel work
assertions: Native transitions execute a bounded cycle and guarded branch.
Nested and parallel child completion obey the parent machine contract.
Parent cancellation and child failure have explicit propagation rules.

cases.title: External structural insertion
assertions: The derived definition waits for approval before the simulated tool.
The original remains unchanged and completes without approval.
Derivation occurs before actor instantiation, not by patching live state.

cases.title: Incompatible targets and conflicts
assertions: Unknown and unsupported targets fail before execution.
Competing insertions fail in either input order instead of silently overwriting.

cases.title: Identity and provenance
assertions: Each occurrence identifies its definition revision and instance.
Added states and connections identify their extension source.
Inspection distinguishes authored definition, resolved definition and actual execution.

cases.title: Targeted human waits
assertions: A wait carries a stable request identity and declared response shape.
Wrong-target, invalid and duplicate responses do not advance another wait.
A human wait differs from a control pause, error and terminal completion.

cases.title: Machine tree restoration
assertions: A serialized snapshot restores parent and child state in new actors.
Restored waits accept the intended response without rerunning completed actions.
Restoration validates the definition revision before execution.

cases.title: Effect uncertainty
assertions: Fault injection covers before effect, after effect and before result persistence.
Idempotency keys suppress duplicate effects where supported.
Uncertain non-idempotent outcomes require explicit reconciliation, not a success claim.

cases.title: Session recovery and settlement
assertions: Transient failures retry within a bounded policy; cancellation aborts retry delay.
Overflow or early final length recovery preserves the failed attempt before repairing model context.
Recovery and queued work finish before the settled event.
Failed recovery does not schedule an unintended internal retry.

cases.title: Fork and branch continuity
assertions: Forked history preserves the original branch.
The selected lineage alone supplies projected context.
An optional branch summary carries abandoned work without importing unrelated raw entries.

cases.title: Interface-independent inspection
assertions: A fresh observer can inspect and respond to a persisted run.
Historical observations differ from current external data.
Parent and child traces retain occurrence and input-output provenance.

cases.title: Stable Agent comparison
assertions: A common simulated scenario compares XState-only orchestration with stable Agent.
Required adapters and behavioral gaps are recorded rather than assumed equivalent.

cases.title: Current Agent comparison
assertions: An isolated compatible XState lane runs the same model-tool scenario.
A custom Pi-compatible executor does not embed another scheduling loop.
Decision, interaction and recovery affordances are evaluated against the common contract.

cases.title: Graph operations
assertions: Union, difference, patching, hierarchy and ports are exercised on the composition fixture.
Identifier collisions and transition identity loss are detected before adoption.
Structural correctness is not treated as behavioral equivalence.

cases.title: Bounded behavior exploration
assertions: Exploration uses finite event samples and explicit bounds.
Reachable snapshots are distinguished from definition nodes and observed traces.
An unbounded or incomplete exploration produces an explicit limitation.

cases.title: Code Mode capabilities
assertions: Injected tools validate arguments and authorize every call.
Code executes only against fixture capabilities under declared limits.
Cancellation and failures leave the host in a defined state.

cases.title: Code Mode replay
assertions: Fixed seed and time plus an ordered host-call journal reproduce the bounded fixture.
A machine snapshot is not treated as a snapshot of an active VM.
Mismatched fingerprints or journal entries reject unsafe replay.

cases.title: Authorized Pi AI smoke
assertions: An explicit approval records provider, credential access, sent data and call limits.
One real model-tool-model round trip uses only fixture tools.
The report records actual usage and differences from simulated behavior without secrets.

cases.title: Real cancellation and control
assertions: A bounded real request responds to cancellation or the agreed control scenario.
Only observed provider behavior is reported as validated; unsupported behavior remains explicit.

cases.title: Summary transport retry parity gap
assertions: The pinned summary helper retries a simulated transient transport error within its configured budget.
The native compaction actor fails after its first failed summary attempt; record a negative parity verdict.
Reference quota failure and cancellation during retry backoff do not issue another request.

cases.title: Automatic post-success compaction parity gap
assertions: The pinned session policy compacts successful responses at threshold or overflow without retrying or omitting the completed answer.
The native recovery parent performs no equivalent post-success compaction; record a negative parity verdict.
The strict threshold boundary is checked as a non-triggering control.

cases.title: Edited context and stale compaction policy gap
assertions: The pinned session policy suppresses recovery for a removed response or stale compaction boundary.
The native recovery input lacks equivalent edit and boundary metadata; demonstrate its ungated recovery and record a negative parity verdict.
A post-response edit invalidates the reference usage estimate and prevents the tested false compaction.
